lesson: Painter remote scripting: a long operation (project.create) called inside the request re-enters the request handler while Painter processes events, so the request runs twice (create succeeds, the second run reports 'already opened'); and create returns before texture sets exist. Queue long operations on the main loop (QTimer.singleShot) and poll a condition - sp_remote.later().

Owner-only Painter set-up works: FBX of owner faces with a BYTE_COLOR 'ID' class attribute -> Painter ID bake from vertex colour, low as high.

lesson: Pilot on frozen UV_Final: (1) measure low->high offsets per pilot face and set extrusion / max_ray_distance from the 5th-95th percentile - roof LP wraps ~0.05 over the tile rolls, 5/78 faces have no high nearby and would stretch the window to +-0.38; (2) OPACITY from highs must be limited to the cutout class (opacity_classes) - solid matb roof faces with missed rays would become holes; (3) horizontal course seams can be added WITHOUT geometry: a bump (constant-height seams, per-column random phase) on a copy of the HIGH's material bakes straight into the normal map.
evidence: 2026-09-28 Texturing_11: pilot_A/B (13 window + 65 roof owners, west hall -X slope), extrusion 0.034 / max_ray 0.231, 35 s per bake; review sheet bake/review/pilot_sheet.png shows rolls (A) and staggered courses + arc joints (B); fixture test extended with the solid-class opacity check and extra UV layers.

lesson: Roof course seams (variant C, owner: vanilla is the floor): model them on how giwa is laid - pan courses as a sawtooth (tile rises to its lower edge, soft lip drop), roll joints on their own rhythm straight across the roll in the slope plane, per-channel stagger +-1/4 course, ~5% wander, per-tile tilt +-30%; MEASURE roll pitch/phase from the HIGH (ray scan) so the pattern sits on the real rolls. Mask the pattern by world normal z (skip vertical eave fronts), never by the angle to one mean slope normal: the roof curves up at the eave and that mask faded the courses exactly where they must continue.
evidence: 2026-09-28 Texturing_11 course_variant.py: roll pitch 0.2745 (5,855 samples); first C mask smoothstep(dot(N, mean n), .72, .80) faded the eave courses; N.z mask (.25-.45) keeps them to the eave with a clean end band; bake/review/pilot_sheet.png A vs C.

The generic QA floor (relative luma std 0.02-0.03) is far below vanilla: vanilla medians are detail energy std(Y-box5)/meanY timber 0.144, plaster 0.046, stone 0.117, roof 0.174.

lesson: Raising one class's density while every other island keeps its exact UV is hole-limited: freed rectangles are exactly the old chart rects, so a merged, larger owner cannot grow beyond the biggest old hole. Free space must be contiguous - re-lay a page that holds only the moving class family (Korean TC: P1024 = roof classes only) instead.

lesson: Roof slopes carry 14-28% covered texels (AO < 0.1: under ridge caps, inside roof intersections). When members share an owner by containment, test that the member's VISIBLE samples never land on the owner's covered samples (<= 1%), otherwise the owner's covered zones print black streaks on visible member roof.

lesson: A procedural bump or ID shader layered on a high-poly must be locked to the features the high already models: measure them first (ray profiles along the slope), and on curved surfaces map through the measured positions piecewise - a period along a straight axis drifts against rows that are even along the curve and bakes a second rhythm.

Bake = two horizontal rhythms; 0.12 = 13 texels (<16). diag: review_checks/diag_hp_R1_sheet.png (geometry vs shader), rows_plot_R1_0.png; fix roof_v2.py (matched filter + per-row refine + piecewise coord), diag_hp_R1D_sheet.png.

Containment gave 175 t/u (+64 % linear) capped only by the 1024 page width.

lesson: Place a motif on a UV island from the surface POS map, not from UV orientation: frame per island n = mean world normal, up = world Z projected into the plane, right = up x n, s,t = world position x 107 tx/unit. It is upright, has runtime size, and keeps its chirality on mirrored islands. Before composing, a distance-to-edge band probe painted into a COPY of BaseColor and rendered via qa_shots image_remap shows which texels the geometry hides (no compose needed).

lesson: Painted ornaments must differ in VALUE from the timber, not only in hue, to read at the RTS camera. Hook shading must go through ctx['shade_mul']: AO written into ctx['ao'] is compressed by the global shade floor (0.45 + 0.55*ao^0.8) and a contact shadow there nearly disappears.

A x1.45 linear value step made the hyeoneo board read as a green mark (rts_before_after_it3.png). A contact ring at 0.5 strength in ao was barely visible in the texel crops; through shade_mul it drew the outline. GABLE_DECOR value_range 0.73 -> 1.00, mid_variation 0.066 -> 0.156.

lesson: A generated ornament scaled to runtime size loses its interior detail: features under ~8 texels (the hyeoneo's spiral curls, ~5 tx at 40 tx tall) survive only as small dark blobs that read like stray glyphs in close renders. The same marks repeat on every gable that uses the motif, and a relief that has no grain inside reads as a flat sticker. Before placing a motif, check its smallest interior feature at runtime size (it must be at least 8 tx), not only its outline.
evidence: DECOR review round 1: uplift_out/DECOR it3 renders west_south/tower_west/tower_east gables show the same brown '13'-like curl marks on a flat teal silhouette; board core normal tilt 0.009-0.011 vs plank 0.05; decor_post.json lists smallest main shape 31.5 tx but the thinnest stroke 1.2 tx

lesson: A carved piece composited onto planks (DECOR hyeoneo board) must not take its colour from the planks under it: flaking scored on the plank joints, a rim made of gable wood x1.35 and paint modulated by the plank luma put the gable's joint lines into the board's BaseColor while its normal (photo plank normal off under the board) shows none, and the rim merges with the gable so the frame disappears. Use the asset's own rim/wood colour and the board's own grain for a separate piece; joint-driven wear only for paint applied directly on the planks.
evidence: DECOR review round 1, 2026-09-28: uplift_out/DECOR P2048 board island x1194 y543, joint texels inside the board luma 52 vs 91 off-joint, normal deviation 0.033 after vs 0.575 before; render zoom of Decor_west_south_gable shows a flat mint-green blob with glyph-like dark marks and no frame.

lesson: Roof bench: mid_variation (blur9-blur33 luma std / mean) is dominated by the tile rhythm itself (0.174 of 0.293 on the owner-approved soft roll/channel light). Per-tile tone barely moves it (+/-15% -> +0.002) and lichen/specks mostly land below 9 or above 33 texels; only channel-correlated darkening raises it, which is exactly a harsher rhythm. Treat mid_variation >= 0.293 as coupled to the waived roll_contrast, not as a weathering target.

lesson: Speck masks must set DENSITY, not amplitude: multiplying a thresholded high-pass by a dirt weight (0..1) leaves grey pepper that never clears an absolute local-contrast bar (dark_frac: Y < blur15 - 0.10). Shift the threshold by the dirt weight and blend each speck fully to the soot colour, applied after lichen/moss so nothing overpaints it.
evidence: Korean TC roof: amplitude-weighted specks dark_frac 0.065-0.080 whatever the threshold; density-shifted full specks 0.097 at the same speck coverage (tune.py runs vs/vt)

lesson: Timber vanilla bar: value_range and mid_variation are won at ZONE scale (painted light via ctx shade_mul on broad under-eave AO, sun-greyed exposed faces, the plank photo's own 5-vs-33 texel board tone opened x1.9), while bright_frac/dark_frac (local +-0.10 vs 15-px blur) cap fine-grain gain - blotchy grime-photo greying or grain gain >1.3 overshoots specks and hue at once. Keep the class mean hue by bisection after local hue shifts (one family).

lesson: Under UV texel sharing, height/facing-driven paint (water-darkened feet, protected undersides, end grain) must use a member-consensus raster: rasterise EVERY face sampling a texel (ridge_faces.json world verts + UV_Final) and take zhi/nz extremes, so a foot darkens only if all members at that texel stand low. Raster z matched the POS bake (median |zhi-z| 1e-4). An offline harness replaying the dumped compose state reproduced the baseline bench exactly, so tuning costs no compose iterations.
evidence: 31% of timber texels shared; 37.5k of 214k low vertical timber texels (17%) share with a higher member -> foot suppressed there; proto.py WOOD bench identical to final/ (value_range 0.8156, detail 0.1558); compose+bench identical to proto on it1-it4.

lesson: Deepening shade/oil by the raw building AO turns a 4-texel AO contact line (gable board under its verge) into a black painted outline around the board; drive zone effects from a 15-texel box of the AO inside the class mask and leave thin contact lines to the global AO.
evidence: CP2/uplift_out/TIMBER/crops/gable_edge_before_it3_it4.png: it3 hard black band on the gable triangles, it4 soft; bench still passes (value_range 1.531).

lesson: Vanilla-bar detail_energy and the speck bands (bright/dark_frac = texels >0.10 sRGB off their 15-texel mean) pull against each other: photo clarity lifts detail but pushes both speck fractions over the vanilla max, and a speck limiter kills detail (most 5x5 energy sits in the strong specks). What passes both: a monotonic grain tone curve on the deviation from the 15-mean (0.1*tanh(g*d/t)/tanh(g) below t=0.1+e, identity above) - fine grain gains contrast while the census over the 0.1 line stays put, e shaves a few specks just over it. Tune it OFFLINE on a dump of the hook inputs (8 s per variant vs 3 min per compose); offline matched the real measure within 0.004 (VR 0.007).
evidence: Claude_CP2/uplift_stone.py + uplift_out/STONE/offline.py; STONE it1 clarity 1.0: detail 0.130 but bright 0.136/dark 0.119 (max 0.108/0.077); limiter knee 0.08: detail 0.097; it4 (curve g=2.0 + fine clarity 3-11): detail 0.125, half 0.115, mid 0.128, VR 1.036, bright 0.072, dark 0.062 - all pass

lesson: Two stone looks the numbers passed but the pictures rejected: (1) a large-band clarity (9-41 texels) on the granite photo turns its mottling into white blotches (mid_variation 0.164, above the vanilla max 0.147 - a ceiling signal even though the bar is a floor); (2) darkening the photo's course joints on floors makes the narrow walkway band read as a ladder of parallel lines (course period ~19 texels, legal by the 16-texel rule, still stripes). Keep floor joints faint and patchy (dirt in some joints only), keep the strong joints on the walls. The stone had NO relief at all (baked normal flat, A_NRM flat): the photo's own roughness map, high-passed with a 13-texel directional line filter, is a clean joint mask for joint darkening and a recessed-joint normal.

lesson: A timber uplift that restores each role's mean HUE can still break the one-timber-family look: greying by blending toward a low-saturation constant drops saturation (GABLE_DECOR 0.53 -> 0.39, WOOD 0.51 -> 0.44) and lifts value, so exposed gable boards drift away from the frozen ridge wood directly above them. Check value AND saturation of each wood role against its frozen neighbours in the render, not only the hue spread; and amplifying the plank photo's dark marks on a light silvered base reads as blotchy grime speckle, not grain.

lesson: Small carved/painted ornaments (~40 tx): paint zones derived from the OUTLINE's distance field inherit every notch of the outline - the hyeoneo's green field came out as a cross, then a keyhole. Derive the painted field from the blurred MASS of the silhouette (box blur ~0.3 x height, cut at a percentile) after a morphological close of the outline, and judge variants at the runtime texel size (x6 nearest), not at the canvas resolution - the canvas zone map looked fine while the 40 tx result was a keyhole.
evidence: decor_gables.py fix round 2026-09-28: uplift_out/DECOR/proto_board_p1..p6.png, proto_zones.png vs proto_variants.png; chosen close 5 tx, blur 12 tx, 36 % mass

lesson: A carved relief normal added by a hook (whiteout) plus the class photo normal (compose nstr) STACK at the ornament's edge: where a plank-joint groove met the board's chamfer the render showed a white hook-shaped highlight outside the board. Cut nstr over the relief's full footprint (alpha dilated by the finite-difference reach, ~1 tx), not over the soft alpha.
evidence: uplift_out/DECOR/after/Close_board_west_south.png r2 it1 (white curl at the lower-right lobe), dbg_board_x12.png normal-deviation map; fix: canvas channel 'foot' = 1 - sstep(-d, 0.3, 1.3)

lesson: A compose hook that blurs in UV space inside the CLASS mask (box of AO or luma) mixes unrelated neighbouring charts: on a thin-chart atlas the zone (under-eave, oiled) and the board-tone boost of thin members are decided by their atlas neighbours, and the vanilla bench rewards that contrast. Blur inside each UV island (island ids rasterised from ridge_faces.json UV_Final) and re-measure the bench on chart-interior texels before trusting a page-level pass.
evidence: TIMBER review r1 (CP2/uplift_out/TIMBER/review_r1/chart_bleed.json, interior_bench.json): hook shade_mul differs from the within-island value by >0.10 on 4.7% of timber texels (p99 0.24); a sunlit +Y strip (building AO 0.89) got light x0.65. Only 26% of WOOD texels are chart-interior (33x33 window >=90% one island); there it4 has mid_variation 0.115 (<0.134), value_range 1.23 (<1.5), detail_half 0.126 (<0.129), bright 0.070 and dark 0.088 above the ceilings, while the page-level bench passes (0.151 / 1.53 / 0.144).

lesson: Tune a compose hook OFFLINE: dump the hook's ctx inputs once (npz), keep the hook's core pure numpy, and replay it in plain python with the benchmark's own class_stats/roof_stats on the rebuilt BaseColor (col * building-AO shade -> sRGB 8 bit). It matches the Blender compose to 1 LSB and costs ~45 s per variant instead of a 3 min compose + measure + render, so the 4 real iterations go to decisions, not to parameter search.
evidence: Korean TC uplift_roof: dump compose byte-identical to final/; ~35 offline variants; estimate vs real gate within 0.002-0.008 (P1024 tile_variation est 0.102 vs real 0.094 = float16 dump + a noisy 7-window median)

lesson: roof_stats tile_variation is a median over the few 128-px windows whose k = sqrt(course*roll period) < 30. Weathering that weakens the lip line's 2nd harmonic flips the detected course period from 16 to its true ~32 texels, so windows drop out (None) or become degenerate (k=29 leaves a 12 px centre, 0.02). On a small page (P1024 roof, 7 windows) the gate then hinges on 1-2 windows. Raise TILE-scale variation (per-tile lichen age, repaired tile groups), not broad zones: bp keeps only 20-40 px structure inside the window centre.
evidence: diag of P1024 windows: before all course 16 / k 23; after it2 course 30-34 in half the windows, median of 7 = 0.094; per-tile lichen age sstep(0.30,0.65) lifted it to 0.100-0.101 (it3/it4)

lesson: A class-wide value_range pass can be bought by one dark geometric band: re-measure the bar with the ground-contact / foot band excluded, and per facing (up vs side), before accepting an uplift.
evidence: STONE uplift it4 (uplift_stone.py): value_range 1.036 vs bar 1.02 on the whole class, but excluding side texels below z 0.15 it drops to ~0.86 and up faces (57% of stone) stay ~0.80; p5 luma falls 0.31 -> 0.21 only because of the foot shade (bottom-10% side texels ~0.12). Up faces barely changed (mean |dRGB| 0.034, normal |dN| 0.005). Review round 1, uplift_out/STONE/review_r1_visual.

lesson: PLASTER vanilla bar: detail_energy_half (>=0.045) is only reachable with a 1-5 texel grain at about +-12 % luma (a photo used as a mask, band-passed and normalised). Geometry layers (frame soiling, streaks, damp) plus procedural trowel strokes top out at 0.035-0.041. The C-photo mid band (6-22 texels) at +-8 % passes too but renders as marble clouds that repeat on every shared panel, so keep mid-scale photo bands under 3 %.
evidence: uplift_out/PLASTER sim sweeps: t1-t3 strokes 0.037-0.038, y2 cband 0.08 0.0435 (render it1 marble stamp), h2/q3 grain 0.12-0.13 0.046-0.050; final it4 0.0475

lesson: value_range (p95-p5)/mean of a plaster class is set by the frame-contact band: 92 % of the darkest 5 % of texels had short-AO contact F>0.5. Deepening the contact colour moved p5 from 0.496 to 0.479. Foot damp, chips and streaks barely moved it. Tune the AO-crevice colour for range, not the dirt layers.
evidence: uplift_out/PLASTER dark-tail analysis (sim g=0.12): F in dark 0.90 vs 0.087 overall; k1 grime 0.95 -> value_range 0.525 -> 0.544

lesson: Boosting a tinted photo's fine band (x1.6) without limiting its dark tail made a photo pit reach luma 0 and the numeric QA failed with an empty texel. Soft-limit the negative side (tanh at 2.5 sigma) and floor the luminance before tinting. A compositor-exact offline simulator (dump the hook ctx once, re-run the hook in numpy plus measure.class_stats) reproduced the benchmark to 4 decimals and saved compose iterations.
evidence: compose_it1: QA FAIL 1 empty texel at P2048 row 842 col 1486 (A rel 0.37 -> lum<0); sim noop matched measure_before 0.0266/0.2504/0.9768

lesson: Free-space share does not mean an unshared chart fits: P2048 at 22.8 % free (fill 0.746) could not take one 300.6 x 35.3 px stone face (A:1862) - the longest free run at 38 px height was 260 px even with no gutter, and no rotation in 3-degree steps fit. Before an evidence phase promises an unshare, run the exact-shape FFT fit (fix_s18e.py try_place) or the longest-free-run test at the chart's own height; long strips are the charts that fail.
evidence: UV_Fix_S18g/fix_report.json skipped[0].diagnosis (longest_free_run 260/250 px, any_angle sweep empty); evidence/stretched notes had claimed the page 'leaves room'

lesson: Review guard for weathering hooks: compare the hook's own change (log luma after/before) with the approved roof's variation, and the tile-pitch autocorrelation before vs after. If the change std is larger than the original std, or the pitch autocorrelation halves, the weathering drowns the approved rhythm and soft light even when the gate improves. Streak or lime columns driven by per-column value noise with a 2-7 texel lattice turn into 1-4 texel barcode stripes and drips on thin strips (eave cut-out rims, hip bands, margins without tile IDs).
evidence: ROOF it4 review r1: change std 0.63 vs original std 0.55/0.51 on ROOF_TILE; lag-30 autocorrelation fell from 0.64-0.74 to 0.27-0.31; 47% of texels changed by more than +-40% in luma; waived roll_contrast rose 1.47 to 2.17 and value_range 0.88 to 1.40; barcode stripes in review_r1/tex_eave_strip.png and tex_tower_hip.png

lesson: Passing the vanilla bar (9/9) does not mean the texture reads as the material. The PLASTER bar for detail_energy_half needs a +-12% 1-5 texel grain. When that grain is spread evenly over the class, it renders as sponge/granite mottle, not lime plaster. Any geometry-driven streak or grain on shared-texel panels is stamped identically on each member. Measure how alike neighbouring shared panels are in the render (best-aligned high-pass correlation) and how much of the column-profile power sits below 16 texels, before accepting.
evidence: Review of the PLASTER uplift it4. In Wall_west_hall_windows the lower panels reach high-pass correlation 0.97/0.92 across neighbours, with high-pass std 0.027 against 0.0065 before, so the stamp is 4x stronger. In the P2048 lowpanel560 column profile, 69% of the power is below 16 texels (std 0.028, 4x before); panel97 has 81% below 16 texels, dominant 12.9 texels. The pavilion render reads as grey granite.

lesson: On shared-texel panels, a geometry band that sits at the right height on every member can still be a stamp. The PLASTER tide line is placed by the owner's height, and Panel_560's 10 members share that height band (dz <= 0.02). But its wiggle comes from the owner's horizontal coordinate and the grime photo, so all members carry the same wavy line. On texels with share > 1, keep foot and streak bands smooth and featureless. Put any irregular shape (tide wiggle, streak columns, stains) only on share == 1 texels, where chips and cracks already are.
evidence: PLASTER it4 review. Wall_west_hall_windows render: 3 adjacent dado panels show the same tide-line wave and the same streak barcode. The high-pass correlation of the upper panels rose from 0.06-0.17 before to 0.34-0.53 after, measured in the render with no alignment. On the P2048 low560 column profile, std rose from 0.0085 to 0.031, with 72% of the power below 16 texels. The stain term still paints share-2 texels at 72% strength (distinct^1.5).

lesson: roof_v2 tile R is independent white noise for pans (seed 11, chan_i,row) and rolls (seed 29, roll_i,row): any per-tile effect keyed on tile R (tone, repaired patches, per-tile lichen cut-off) cuts at the pan/roll boundary and draws rectangles - the owner-rejected two-grid read. Key per-tile weathering on (course row, roll index) shared by pan and roll, or keep it as gentle as the approved +-12%.
evidence: Review r1 of uplift_roof.py it4: texel crop P2048 rear hall (rolls horizontal) shows rectangular lichen/tone blocks ending at pan/roll edges; roof_v2.py build() EMIT mode; roll_contrast 1.47->2.17 despite the owner waiver for a softer read.

lesson: A carved bevel in a hook's tangent normal reads as a DARK OUTLINE on every side when it is steep (~40-45 deg after texel averaging): with the review sun ~51 deg off the wall normal, tilting away drops N.L to ~0.1 while tilting toward the light only lifts it 0.63 -> 0.9, so the lit sides barely brighten. Proven with a 4-patch probe (+-U, +-V tilts painted into a copy of the normal, rendered through image_remap): the orientation was correct, only the asymmetry was the problem. For readable raised ornaments keep bevels <= ~30 deg (height 1.1 tx over a 1.4 tx chamfer) and do not blame the tangent space before probing it.

lesson: Text on a texture island: set glyphs from an installed font offline (PIL; Blender's Python has none) into a mask at 16 samples/texel, then place them in the hook by the face's exact UV->world affine and a world frame (right = up x n). That keeps the text upright and unmirrored even on a UV island rotated 180 deg. Snap each glyph to the texel grid with a sub-texel offset search (minimum half-tone) and count frame bands in whole texels from the edge (floor of the distance). This gives crisp 1-texel lines at 107 tx/unit. A flat-nib dilation (1.15 tx at 18 deg) turns a thin Ming face (SimSun) into bold brush strokes and keeps a dense character (車) open at 24 tx.
evidence: Claude_CP2/decor_nameboard.py; uplift_out/NAMEBOARD/after/Name_board_texel.png (軒東 upright, right-to-left); pos deviation of the affine vs the POS map 0.0013 u; QA PASS

lesson: Before painting decoration onto a baked element, measure texel sharing by rasterising EVERY plan face's UV polygon on the page and intersecting it with the target's texels; do not infer sharing from identical-looking bakes. The Korean TC window/door panels were reported as 'all 13 share texels' - the S18f plan shows each of the 13 WINDOW_ASSEMBLY owners owns its texels (family_size 1) and only Panel_1618 (two tower upper-storey faces) is shared; they look alike because all were baked from one HIGH panel bank.

lesson: Placing a painted motif on a baked sub-panel (door lower panel): build the face's exact affine UV->(s right, t up) map from its own 4 vertices, sample the BAKED normal on that upright grid and read the relief lines - the HIGH panel sits at a different offset in every LOW quad (leaf joint at s 53..69 over six doors), so fixed fractions miss. Gotchas: the leaf-gap lines run full height while the inset's side lines stop at the inset foot (take the highest foot, not the median); modelled hardware (METAL knobs in front of the leaf) crowds a centred motif - measure it in the same frame and move the pair down just enough, one height per facade so the row stays level.

lesson: Weathering loudness has a numeric proxy that matches reviewer rejection: std of the hook's linear log-luma change vs the surface's own log-luma std. Pair it with tile-pitch autocorrelation (keep >= ~0.9x before) and darker30/brighter40 shares (< 10%).

lesson: The vanilla-bar roof metrics detail_energy(_half), bright/dark_frac, roll_peak_db and mid_variation cannot be met on the owner's soft grey giwa without texel-level pepper or a harsher rhythm: they measure fine texture/roll contrast that the owner's waived look lacks. Soft, believable weathering moves them by <0.01-0.02; chasing them produced the rejected grunge. Take them to the owner as a waiver decision, not a tuning target.

lesson: A texel hook's high-frequency change at chart borders becomes gutter barcode after the compositor's dilate fill; smoothing the hook's log-factor with a masked blur inside a 4-texel band along the gutter (and keeping specks out of it) returns gutter neighbour differences to near the approved level.

When a compose hook replaces a bake-only class's relief inside a sub-region by design (e.g. window frame chamfers), export that region as a mask and scope stacked_normal_check with it; unscoped, the detector fails the whole class.

lesson: Texel-space painting per face must use a concave-safe polygon test: the min-over-half-planes signed distance silently empties concave faces (column faces notched by rails, 12 corners), dropping 25 % of the paint and whole column bands. Use even-odd inside + distance to the nearest edge, and an affine UV->world map from the best-conditioned corner triangle.

lesson: Member-consensus rasters (a band that must sit at the top of EVERY face sharing a texel) must only count faces whose OWN UV polygon covers the texel: a family can hold several owner faces (one chart = 8 octagon sides), and extrapolating another owner's UV->world map onto foreign texels returns garbage depths.
evidence: Korean TC DANCHEONG it2: pavilion column bands came out partial and run-order dependent (band count 210 in it1, 0 in it2 for the same family); fixed with a coverage test per face (decor_dancheong.apply band branch)

A monotonic decay with no local peak below lag 16 proves no short-period repeat; the approved tile rhythm in the base image cannot mask or fake it.

lesson: To triangulate an export copy exactly as Blender tessellates it (viewport, bake), use the Triangulate modifier with quads FIXED and ngons CLIP; ngons BEAUTY picks different diagonals.

lesson: Verify a converter GR2 read-back by whole triangles (position+UV of all three corners, both directions), not per vertex with a loose UV tolerance: the --bang conversion welds same-position corners whose UVs differ by < ~1e-3.

Every GXO vertex still equals some Blender corner exactly, so the dryrun's per-vertex check (UV tol 1e-3) reported all matched.

lesson: The converter's GR2->GXO/FBX dump applies each file's ArtToolInfo (axis vectors and UnitsPerMeter), so equal GXO frames of a raw-built GR2 and a converter-built (Oodle1) GR2 do not prove equal raw/engine frames; only a raw read or the game settles it.
evidence: Copies of korean_tc_pilot.gr2 with ArtToolInfo patched in place (CRC recomputed): RightVector (-1,0,0)->(1,0,0) makes the GXO exactly the x-negated original; UnitsPerMeter 1.5625->1.0 scales the GXO by 1.5625. The pilot's ATI (Right -X, Up +Y, Back +Z, UPM 1.5625) reproduces its dump map raw = 2.54*(-gx, gz, -gy) exactly. Converter-written files are Oodle1 and their ATI is unreadable here, so journal 2026-09-28-claude-79 (x-mirror) rests on an assumption until the in-game check.

lesson: A long linear element that carries a directional pattern (ridge cap-tile row, beam, rail, eave strip) must be ONE continuous UV strip along its run with one orientation; QA needs a continuity check per element (islands per run, orientation, pattern phase across seams) - member registration and density checks do not catch scattered runs.

lesson: An analytic per-segment texture on a thin faceted tube (side ridge, 15 texels wide) fails even when UV registration is perfect: a box-ridge model (base band + course joints) painted onto 6-8 texel side facets makes two pale pinstripes that read as white at mip 1-3; rule classes cut by smooth baked normals (nu>0.35) run through facet middles; per-FRAME random phase and per-segment h0 jump the pattern at every joint; painted bake margins (h extrapolated < base) are white and bleed. Paint a tube as ONE element-continuous cap row keyed to facet identity, with >= 4-texel features and neutral margins.
evidence: UV_Fix_S18h/diagnose/texture: E06 (west-hall south gable west verge) 32/35 owner faces, J~identity; outer side facets lum 104->111 over mips vs cap 75, roof 64; hip-chart margin 54% BASE lum 140; 55/59 joints lap-phase jump > 2 texels; cap/side rule boundary normal crease median 12.5 deg vs cap interior 1.6

lesson: Measure scatter per 3D RUN, not per chart: on the Korean TC every side ridge (verge + hip, one continuous 7-face tube, 2.4-2.8 m) is cut at the verge/hip kink into two strips packed in different page blocks, plus 3 single-face islands (top cap, first-hip UNDER, eave cap) that all 12 runs share. Each strip is perfect on its own (105-110 t/u, aniso <=1.08, straight, continuous over bends), registration of members passes (<=2 deg, <=0.9 texel) - so density, overlap and role-registration gates all pass while the run is scattered. Gate: islands per run (target 1 + caps), page path island->island vs run length (target ~1x), same +s direction and handedness across every seam of the run.
evidence: UV_Fix_S18h/diagnose/uv (ridge_uv_diag.py, ridge_uv_summary.json): 12 side ridges, 413 faces -> 59 islands (12 if one strip each); verge->hip strip gap 166-695 px (median 471) on P1024, 5/12 mirrored, 3/12 turned 90/180; page path 3.3-5.1x the run length; largest island holds 54-61 % of the run; S18g identical on all 595 ridge faces. Painter side: 173/191 UV-continuous segment joints still jump 2-4.6 texels because ridge_eave.py paints in per-straight-segment 3D frames.

It also names the element for certain - the owner's circled 'rear hall' side ridge was the WEST hall south gable west verge + SW hip (ridge frames 33-37).

lesson: A round side ridge (6-face hexagonal tube, 5-7 texels per face at 107 t/u) painted by a per-texel rule (smoothed world normal nu>0.35 = cap, else stacked courses + lime joints + lime foot line) reads as a grey metal pipe with white rails and rivet ticks: the class boundary cuts through faces, the lime joints land on the lower flanks at heights measured from each straight segment's own frame so the pale line jumps at every bend, and the island gutters are pale (lum 0.44 vs 0.31 inside) so filtering adds white edges. lesson: Weathering on plaster must be a SOFT density, never a threshold. Thresholding the grime photo's grain inside weathering zones (rain streaks, the band under the beam, the damp foot) left dark hard-edged clumps. They read as camouflage or a ruin, and along one panel edge as glyph-like marks. A soft density whose tone is broken by the photo's 1-2 texel pores, and by grain drawn out along the flow on unshared texels only, reads as a rain wash like vanilla CN plaster. The clean lime between zones stays smooth.
evidence: uplift_out/PLASTER sim r2final vs s2e crops (pavilion, side3_up, panel96): r2final dep = sstep(gran + 2.6*(M-0.55)) gave dark clumps and letter-like marks on panel96; s2e dep = M*clip(1+1.3*pore+0.7*flow) gave directional washes with pore speckle. Unshared luma 0.759 -> 0.790, shared high-pass 0.0196 -> 0.0165 (baseline 0.0191).

lesson: The Korean TC AO bake is short-range contact AO. It cannot tell a wall sheltered under a roof from an exposed one, so it cannot weight rain streaks by exposure: the pavilion core wall under the upper roof reads ao 1.00, the same as open exterior panels. To keep sheltered walls free of rain wash, bake a sky-visibility (long-range, upper-hemisphere) AO first. Do not proxy exposure by height.
evidence: uplift_out/PLASTER dump_P2048 medians: pavilion core ao 1.00 / aos 1.00, exterior Panel_97 ao 0.99, tower Side3 ao 0.96, lower Panel_560 ao 0.95 (10th pct 0.75-0.88 everywhere).

lesson: Side-ridge run strips (Korean TC S18h design): one straight crown-centred strip per run is feasible within the density gate. Mapping every joint ring to one V line at the centreline arc length (ring edges at their exact length) gives along-density 102.1-111.0 t/u (target 107) even across the 28-35 deg verge-to-hip bend - the mitre effect is r*tan(bend/2)/segment length = 0.022/0.6, under 5 %. Topology facts that an unroller must respect: the tube is open at the bottom on hip segments 2-3 (6 faces); UNDER faces exist only on verge 1-2 and hip 1; the first verge's side faces are pentagons; the tower lower hips' last classify 'segment' holds two rings (14 faces), so rings must be found by topology (edge loops), never by projection clusters (projection clustering gave 197 t/u there). Anchor the 0.27 cap pitch at the eave end (as built, cut the top tile) so congruent runs get identical laps; per-run integer pitches gave 0.258 vs 0.283 on two runs 4 mm apart in length.
evidence: scratchpad run_geom.py + ngon_check.py on ridge_faces.json / plan_final_pages_S18g.json: 16 runs, owned area 177k px2 (16.9 % of P1024), strip bbox 53 x 333 px for the 12 gable-hip runs; frames 33-37 face lists (A:845/A:850 5-gons, A:851/A:844/A:3130 UNDER, frames 36-37 without UNDER)

lesson: Decoration on conjoined UVs: audit texel sharing by UV-polygon OVERLAP groups, not by plan family. A multi-owner chart family holds owners with separate texels; a family-level 'one recipe' check blocked every rafter (end face vs side faces in one chart) although no texel was shared.
evidence: DANCHEONG it5: family audit dropped 68/80 rafters and 13/13 beam lines; overlap groups (sd>0.25 texel sets) left 5 raw faces in the whole building (decor_dancheong.py share_groups).

lesson: Element-level all-or-nothing painting collapses on this model: the conjoinment shares bracket-set and beam texels ACROSS sets and buildings (one column-head group serves 12 sets; west-hall beams share with rear-hall and tower beams), so dropping one set/ring cascades to all. Keep atomicity only for independent large elements (shafts, railing, per beam line) and resolve sets per face, listing the raw faces.
evidence: it5 resolve(): set-atomic -> 26/27 sets dropped; ring-atomic -> 13/13 lines dropped; per-line + per-face sets -> 10/13 lines, 27 sets, 5 raw faces.

lesson: RTS read at 50 deg: eave-hidden decoration (brackets, column heads) changes < 300 px per 800x520 frame; painting what the camera sees (pavilion columns + railing, veranda columns) changes 4-5k px. Check render_diff at the RTS cameras before judging decoration.
evidence: DANCHEONG it4 73-284 px vs it5 4070-5299 px changed (>24) per RTS frame, render_diff_it5.json.

lesson: A distance field built by a capped walk (texels to the frame above, cap kmax) goes flat past the cap. Any exp(-d/L) effect then leaves a constant residual over the rest of a tall panel. In PLASTER, rain streaks ran the whole height of the pavilion core wall at 0.1-0.18 below 120 texels. Give every effect driven by a capped distance a hard end below the cap (1 - smoothstep(d, 1.1L, 1.9L) with L < cap/1.9), and dump the distance and length arrays on the tallest panel before trusting a decay.

lesson: In a compose hook, a class mask (cls == X & valid) does NOT separate UV islands: the surface bake margin carries the class label, so plaster islands 4 texels apart are one connected mask. Box filters and frame walks masked by class then leak a neighbour island's frame soiling onto an open edge. Mask every box, walk and crack by a chart label (components of the rasterised plan faces, margins assigned to the nearest chart), not by the class.

Frame walks crossed into another island on 221 shared texels.

lesson: Arris wear in a paint hook must come from real geometry (compose edge / dihedral), never from the distance to each face's own UV polygon edge. A round column is 8 facet strips about 6 texels wide in one continuous chart; per-polygon chipping puts a line of chips on every facet split. The result is a regular dashed stripe every ~6 texels along each column, which is a repeated pattern under 16 texels on edges that are not arrises. Coplanar beam splits get the same treatment.

lesson: A welded straight strip for a mitred ridge tube must NOT map each ring to one V line: the Korean TC verge rings are vertical cuts (30-45 deg off the tube's cross-section), so V=const per ring sheared the side faces to fit-anisotropy 1.88 and 147 t/u across. Map V = TPU*(s_ring + axial offset of the vertex along the ring's bisector axis) and U = ring-edge length measured perpendicular to that axis: fit-anisotropy drops to <=1.23 (tri 1.36), density 104-111. Measure UV distortion per triangle, not with a planar affine fit: twisted thin quads make the fit report 118 t/u where the triangles say 108.

lesson: A compose hook for one element must be scoped by the element's OWNER UV polygons, not by an ID bake alone: every surface bake's EXTEND margin (RIDGE_ID, CLS and the per-class sources) of a neighbouring chart overwrites the element's polygon-edge texels. On the Korean TC side ridges 302 owner texels (32 faces) carried eave RIDGE_ID codes and EAVE_CUTOUT class, so the hook skipped them and the compositor's eave source gave 1-2-texel lighter lines. Fix = scope (ID mask | polygon mask), take the per-texel source inputs (clay/plaster photo, grime, dirt) of those texels from the nearest in-polygon texel of the element, and claim free gutter texels (in no other owner's polygon) that are strictly nearer to the element's polygons (ring distance), since bilinear filtering reads them at the face edge.

lesson: Blender's EXTEND bake margin also fills MISSED-ray texels inside a selected-to-active receiver (a miss unmasks the texel), so every direct OPACITY/NORMAL bake shrinks its holes by 'margin' texels per side and NORMAL/EMIT/AO holes carry extended neighbour values. A bake master must therefore bake with margin 0 (exact hit mask); derive re-applies the target recipe's margin with the same EXTEND rule, misses left unassigned.

Measure every member's t/u and anisotropy against the target before recommending a conjoin as the fix; a conjoin can fail the exact check an unshare was rejected for.

lesson: Pixel checks through img.pixels depend on the datablock's colorspace when the file is 16-bit: Blender loads a 16-bit PNG into a float buffer and linearizes it unless the image is Non-Color, so two datablocks of the SAME file give different means. 8-bit images read the stored values either way. Compare pixel values only on Non-Color / byte images (or read the file itself), never assume img.pixels = file values.

lesson: Painting a lattice ON a baked lattice: never regularise it in paint. Folding narrow baked cells and the bars beside them into a frame member, or splitting a cell with a painted bar, puts flat paint over baked bars (they show through as dark / light hairlines) and over flat paper (a painted bar with no relief), and it made a 27 cm red band out of a 5-texel meeting stile. Paint every baked member as baked: bars in the bar colour, narrow cells stay paper, the meeting stile keeps its width, the rails keep the bar colour where their relief crosses the meeting stile and where they run into the stiles (measure it on the page Normal first: an ASCII map of flat / edge texels). A metric the base already fails (class_pattern of the bake's own strips) is not a reason to repaint the bake.

Pull a written sheet by STRUCTURE: paper level = grey closing wider than a stroke, ink = darker than its LOCAL paper + not red + stroke-sized + not within a margin of the sheet edge; lift and floor the paper field (hanji yellows, it does not char); clip non-ink marks. lesson: Subdividing baked cells into an inner grid: never choose the count per cell by rounding alone, and never by an evenness optimiser per instance. Per-cell rounding split the bake's 22 | 23 texel twins either side of a meeting stile into 4 | 5 columns (mirror leaves differ) and 20 | 21 texel rows into 2 | 3 rows on neighbouring windows; a per-instance 'most even openings' search picked square 4-5 texel rows and still differed between the tower's side-by-side windows. What works: group the cells by length (a new group where the next cell is > group_tx longer, 5 on the column axis), one fixed rounding rule on the group mean with a target from the harness drawing, and a target scale that keeps every real cell height clear of a count threshold (check the fractional part of (W+m)/(o+m) for all baked sizes, not just the look).

lesson: A 1-texel painted line gets its relief on its NEIGHBOUR texels: any symmetric profile inside the line's own texel box-filters to a flat normal. Height 1 on the line, central differences on the texel grid (crest flat, one shoulder texel each side tilted H/2 per texel), neighbours outside the allowed region count as the texel itself (no slope toward baked bars), then Reoriented Normal Mapping onto the bake (never add / overwrite). Read the tangent convention off the bake itself before writing slopes (a rail's lower edge -y, its right edge +x = OpenGL +Y with the compose's bottom-up rows). 2 mm on a 9.35 mm texel = slope 0.107: clear on the Normal board, only a faint light/shade edge in lit close-ups, invisible at the RTS/owner camera; the class-wide stacked-normal ratio (0.187) does not flag it, so report the relief texels on their own.

lesson: Scoped-edit gates are only as strong as their weakest trust anchor. The breaker got 12 of 12 out-of-scope changes past layers.py on the synthetic store. (1) Owner decisions: anyone can write one with state.py decision add, any baseline name counts as one, and none is bound to the layer or state it approves. (2) render_preflight and publish.py candidate trust a writable LAYER.json. (3) promote --expect-state accepts any state, not only HEAD. (4) The gutter zone W takes empty texels that dilate() fills from a NEIGHBOUR's face (band W: 12,233 texels touching timber_rest = the green ledge). (5) Two layer applies race and lose an accepted layer (no compare-and-swap on HEAD). (6) A direct-mode submit from a stale copy reverts a --supersedes layer inside the scope. (7) A conflicting candidate stays previewable. (8) Renders and Preview load P*_AO/P*_Metallic from final/. Rules: bind every gate to pixels plus the store, never to a file an agent can write; W = the texels whose dilate source is the scope; HEAD moves by CAS on the old id.
evidence: scratchpad/scoped_breaker/test_breaker.py (12 passed = 12 holes); measure_real.json (real plan, gutter_steps 10)
